Skia / Metal and Core Graphics on the Cintiq

Matched synthetic input and native canvas conditions. Read ordinary short-stroke behavior first, then stress cases and completion outcomes.

Short strokesFirst markOverlap stressSustainedFailuresRecommendationEvidence

Physical pen-to-screen latency remains pending

Endpoint: Scheduled sample → first draw start. This is neither drawing completion nor visible ink. Generated 240 Hz replay bypasses Wacom digitizer and driver delivery. A suitable camera is still required to measure physical pen movement through visible pixels. Neither backend is declared a physical-latency winner.

Coverage: complete-with-failures

372 attempted in the retained matrix of 372 declared runs; 368 accepted; 4 classified failed observations; 0 pending; 0 invalid.

Acceptance means software artifact validation; image quality and native inspection remain separate review gates. Missing cells are shown as pending, never estimated. Failed runs are excluded from accepted percentiles, so completion counts must be read alongside timings.

Software comparison complete: 372 planned outcomes

All 360 primary runs and 12 sustained runs have a validated outcome: 368 accepted and four classified Core Graphics sustained failures, in 186 matched pairs. There are no pending or invalid entries in the final retained matrix. Historical rejected attempts remain preserved separately. All 360 primary-matrix runs completed; 182 pairs support numeric comparisons and four sustained pairs retain a completed Skia run alongside a failed Core Graphics run.

The frozen native binary and measurement rules stayed unchanged across recovery sessions. Acquisition finished on 15 October 2026, and the original display mirroring was restored. Physical pen-to-screen acquisition remains pending suitable camera equipment and a real-pen input adapter; this generated replay does not measure the Pro Pen 3 digitizer or driver.

Recommendation: develop Skia next, retain Core Graphics as a lightweight baseline

For this editable infinite-canvas app, prioritize Skia/Metal for the next implementation and real-pen experiment. Its much smaller dense-scene backlog and six completed sustained stress runs outweigh its several-millisecond drawing-start disadvantage in the simpler cached scenes. This is an engineering recommendation for the tested implementation, not proof of earlier visible ink, a universal renderer ranking, or permanent backend approval.

The tradeoff is real. On the larger cached empty canvas, median run p95 scheduled-to-first-draw-start delay is 10.71 ms for Skia versus 7.44 ms for Core Graphics. With 5,000 committed strokes and the same short-stroke trace, it is 18.62 ms versus 1,014.97 ms. Each value summarizes five accepted runs. Both rebuild caches synchronously; large rebuilds and deferred app-side rasterization can block delivery even when Core Graphics draw callbacks look short.

For 30-second repeated-overlap strokes on the larger cached canvas, the same p95 summary is 40.26 ms for Skia versus 460.01 ms for Core Graphics. These repeated curves and abrupt position resets are an adversarial fixture, not typical pen motion. Pan/zoom plus this ink trace gives 19.07 ms versus 94.74 ms.

Across six 180-second sustained trials, Skia completed six; Core Graphics completed two and failed four, with 1,056–3,777 input samples never drawn in failed runs. The two completed Core Graphics runs reached finish entry at 222.764 seconds (smaller) and 218.592 seconds (larger) for a 180-second replay. Accepted therefore does not mean on-time: the cooperative watchdog cannot preempt long main-thread drawing. The completed run at each size still has p95 delays of 14.46 seconds (smaller) and 21.19 seconds (larger). Skia’s median run p95 is 294.87 ms and 304.66 ms respectively: it also needs substantial long-stroke optimization. Completion alone is not responsive drawing.

Next, bound live-stroke geometry work and cache-rebuild cost, then rerun matched trials. Retain Core Graphics for a simpler bounded-content viewer or minimal-dependency option. Skia adds engine size and GPU integration complexity; this experiment does not remove those costs. Measure actual pen-to-visible-ink before claiming a latency winner, and keep production selection subject to owner approval.

Resource tradeoff: for the larger cached empty canvas, median measured app CPU time is 7.78 s for Skia versus 13.40 s for Core Graphics over the 30-second replay; process-lifetime peak RSS is 268.75 versus 753.14 MiB. For the larger cached 5,000-stroke scene, these are 14.44 versus 30.87 CPU seconds and 1,470.28 versus 1,546.39 MiB. RSS includes initialization and untimed capture; CPU excludes external WindowServer and GPU work. These are descriptive process costs, not total graphics memory or energy. Sustained Skia runs also reached multi-gigabyte RSS, so completion is not a memory-efficiency endorsement.

Hardware, matching and timing boundaries

Measured native binary: source 8a26d1d7a25bfcbc526584d386a4f49c30ecbbcf, SHA-256 9e7ad2880182ab4ea5416cff763f417fde59a31dab4a992d1d0faad27cb2c16d. Final collection frozen separately at collector revision 1dcdb92; runner/analyzer content is unchanged from acabb64. Earlier retained outcomes preserve their original receipts and session provenance. Apple M2 Pro with 19 GPU cores; macOS 27.0.1 (26A434); Cintiq Pro 22, 3840×2160 physical pixels, 1920×1080 points, nominal 120 Hz. Measured canvases are 1600×1000 and 2560×1600 physical pixels. The Sony secondary display was unmirrored during retained trials.

Both adapters consume the same timestamped generated 240 Hz trace through shared Rust editing and geometry. Both use the same application-controlled R full-redraw or C cached-base-plus-live policy, synchronous cache replacement, canvas dimensions and input-preservation rules. The replay bypasses Wacom digitizer and driver delivery; Pro Pen 3 is owner-reported, not characterized by these trials.

The primary delay ends at the start of the first drawing callback representing each input sample. It excludes the remainder of drawing, deferred rasterization, composition, scanout and pixel response. All-sample delays expose backlog that latest-sample age alone can hide. A nominal 120 Hz mode and Metal callbacks do not measure photons.

Verification and diagnostic evidence

The integration check, 20 experiment tests, strict experiment Clippy and release build passed at native revision 8a26d1d. All 49 portable analysis/report tests passed after report integration at f3dc920. The final report narrative changes are checked separately; native measurements are never relabeled as a report-only revision.

Fifty-six separately identified two-second visual/ledger pilots passed at native revision 8756358: seven workload cases, two canvas sizes, both policies and both backends. Within each backend, R/C final images were byte-identical for all 28 matched pairs. Cross-backend edge antialiasing differs; scene geometry, orientation, scale and clipping were inspected rather than demanding pixel identity.

Native inspection at 8a26d1d covered Ready/Completed states, both physical canvas sizes, Run, Escape, Command-period cancellation, Command-Q preservation/exit and Show Results availability. A designer reviewed source, screenshots and those observations. Dark appearance, complete keyboard focus traversal, physical pen feel and temporal cache handoff appearance remain unverified.

Three paired logging-overhead trials per backend and four native Stop tests passed in separate preflight evidence. Full-versus-minimal CPU differences were small and mixed; this does not prove zero logging overhead. Every comparative run uses full logging.

An excluded 90-second diagnostic at the same native revision sampled the stalled Core Graphics main thread in backing-store/display-list rasterization and antialiasing edge distribution. This explains why short draw callbacks can coexist with high process CPU and input backlog. The profile is diagnostic, not an additional comparative timing trial. Process CPU includes app-side deferred rasterization but excludes WindowServer CPU and GPU execution.

A fresh independent final-data assessment reproduced the final analysis exactly, verified every retained artifact across recovery sessions5–8 and all 80 first-mark rows against raw samples, deliveries and frames, and confirmed one exact dual-display stratum for all 372 outcomes. The final 49 analysis/report tests and 12 first-mark/report tests pass. The designer reviewed final report source and screenshots; final browser checks cover desktop and narrow layouts. Native measurements retain their original source revision.

Recovery history and evidence retention

Six environmental attempts were rejected and preserved: session1 Dock overlay; session3 Sony display configuration change; session4 Window Server overlay; session5 Dock overlay; session6 locked-screen startup before manifest creation; session7 full-window occlusion, confirmed by the owner covering the window or switching desktops. Session2 ended on the first performance failure before the explicit continuation amendment. Session8 completed the remaining matrix. An accepted but unpaired Skia run from session3 remains excluded; that pair was repeated in full.

All four classified sustained failures are preserved as failures and were not retried. Input completeness, final expected hashes, artifact receipts and paired identities passed the frozen continuation policy. Other failures and visibility changes halt acquisition. The coverage counter describes the final retained matrix, not every historical attempt. Accepted sustained runs can finish late because the main-thread watchdog is cooperative and cannot preempt a long callback; completion is not a deadline guarantee.

Raw ledgers, receipts, manifests, images, all eight collection sessions, recovery records and separate preflight/profile evidence remain in local artifacts. The analysis contains every retained outcome, pair, uncertainty summary and frozen provenance. Secondary first-mark evidence covers all 80 accepted first-use/after-idle runs and is bound to the final analysis checksum. Previously stopped bundle-size checks remain pending.

1. Ordinary short-stroke traces

Separate 0.75-second strokes. Cached rendering is shown first; full redraw is a control. Warm, first-painter-use and after-idle runs, and the two physical canvas sizes, stay separate. “Ordinary” describes this generated trace shape, not a measurement of real pen feel. First-painter-use values summarize the full 30-second replay and can dilute a one-time first-mark cost; reference construction and context initialization precede that replay epoch. These are not cold-launch-to-visible-ink measurements.

First measured mark: secondary software evidence

The first expected sample is tracked through its delivery batch to the first draw that represents it. This avoids hiding a one-time delay inside a whole-run p95. Values below are medians across five runs per backend and condition; they are not physical contact-to-ink timings. First painter use has no warm-up; after-idle follows warm-up and a 30-second idle period.

The endpoint is drawing start: it excludes the first frame’s drawing work, deferred rasterization and display. First-use measurements begin after replay/reference and context initialization, not at app launch. After-idle sub-millisecond values are therefore not sub-millisecond visible ink.

2. Repeated-overlap stress: 30 seconds

Long traces and the ink portion of pan/zoom traces follow a repeated curve with abrupt end-to-start position resets. A 30-second long trace makes 15 passes. These are repeated-overlap stress cases, not representative smooth motion or spatially growing lines. Their scales are independent of ordinary short strokes.

3. Sustained stress and paired completion: 180 seconds

The sustained trace retraces the same path 90 times with abrupt position resets. Completion is an outcome alongside software timing. Accepted means complete validated artifacts, not a deadline guarantee: the cooperative main-thread watchdog cannot preempt a long drawing callback. Three declared pairs per size provide limited evidence; failed members contribute no accepted timing distribution or numeric paired difference.

Failure gaps include the censored interval from the last draw to finish entry. Undrawn sample ages are measured at that endpoint, not photons or observed first-draw latencies. Failed runs are excluded from accepted percentiles. Empty failure tables mean no classified failure in this analysis, not proof that every pending run will succeed.

Recommendation and remaining decision

Among 14 fully paired ordinary cached conditions, Skia has the lower median paired run-p95 in 2; Core Graphics in 12; the remainder tie. This counts condition-level directions without pooling percentiles or inventing a latency budget. Inspect effect sizes and completion outcomes above before deciding whether differences matter.

No uniformly resolved software advantage across ordinary cached conditions. There is no universal winner in these short-stroke cells. The dense-content and sustained evidence supports prioritizing Skia development; retain Core Graphics as the baseline for a future physical comparison.

Synchronous cache replacement queues incoming input during rebuilds in both adapters. Asynchronous replacement is deferred. Physical pen-to-screen latency remains pending a suitable camera regardless of software results.

ApproachAdvantagesCosts and limits
Skia / MetalExplicit GPU submission and separate Metal observations; potential renderer reuse across platforms.Additional bundled engine and GPU resources. Drawable waits and queueing matter; Metal callbacks do not measure photons.
AppKit / Core GraphicsSystem drawing API and native AppKit integration without bundling Skia.Drawing can be deferred beyond callback return. A short draw callback omits deferred rasterization. Process CPU includes work performed in this app, but excludes WindowServer CPU and GPU execution.

Measured process CPU and callback wall time

Process user and system CPU sum execution across all process threads from the measured replay epoch to finish entry. They exclude initialization, warm-up, idle, GPU retirement, capture and artifact serialization. External WindowServer CPU and GPU execution are not included. Draw callback totals are synchronous wall durations including drawable waits and painter calls; they are not CPU utilization. RSS is process-lifetime peak memory including initialization and untimed capture, excluding distinct GPU/WindowServer allocations. Missing values remain unknown (—), never zero. These are descriptive measurements, not energy estimates.

Skipped drawing snapshots are not lost input samples: acceptance requires every expected sample in the delivery ledger and a subsequent first drawing representation. Frame input timing fields are not summed as Rust work; host aggregate advance totals are retained. Final captures are untimed painter/readback proxies, not proof of presented pixels. OS visibility flags do not establish absence of every partial occluder. Visibility checks run on the main queue and can miss transient occlusion while that queue is blocked; they are not continuous proof of visibility. A nominal display refresh rate is not an observed pen-to-screen latency or a performance budget.
